newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL FALLS ON RATING, GAS PRICE UNCERTAINTY.
newsitem.headline: MOL FALLS ON RATING, GAS PRICE UNCERTAINTY.

text.p: The shares in Hungarian oil and gas company MOL Rt opened lower on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Thursday but traders said a "sell" rating by ABN AMRO Hoare Govett was not the only factor.
MOL shares opened at 1,905 forints, below Wednesday's close of 1,930. At 1113 GMT MOL shares stood at 1,915 forints.
"I wouldn't say the price fall stems from ABN AMRO's rating only," a salesman told Reuters. "MOL shares are bought on the SEAQ at prices of around 1,910 and 1,915 forints."
"What I would say is that the market is rather divided about the size of the wholesale gas price increase."
ABN AMRO Hoare Govett this moring rated MOL shares as "sell" saying they reached a price level which is too high.

Tommy Erdei, analyst at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said the price rise came on speculation concerning the forthcoming announcement by the government on the attribution of the gas price increases between MOL and distribution companies.

The Hungarian government announced in late November that it would raise retail gas prices by 18.8 percent and electricity prices by 24.9 percent. However, it has released few details, giving rise to speculation.
